en: Your human arm acts as a third-class lever, meaning your bicep must exert much more force than the weight of the object you are lifting.
A single fixed pulley does not multiply your lifting force, but it makes work easier by allowing you to pull downward instead of upward.
The pressure from ice skates melts a microscopic layer of ice into water, creating the slippery lubrication that allows you to glide.
If you weigh exactly 100 pounds on Earth, you would weigh only 38 pounds on Mars because its gravitational pull is much weaker.
Dropping a permanent magnet repeatedly on a hard floor can destroy its magnetism because the physical shock scrambles its aligned magnetic domains.
Pure water is actually an electrical insulator that cannot conduct electricity until impurities like salt or minerals are dissolved into it.
Ambulances paint their front logos backwards because flat mirrors reverse images left-to-right, making the word appear correctly spelled in the driver's rearview mirror.
Sound waves travel about four times faster in water than in air because liquid water molecules are packed much more closely together.
Black asphalt roads get significantly hotter than white concrete sidewalks under the sun because dark colors absorb more radiant heat energy.
A metal spoon placed in hot soup quickly becomes too hot to touch because metals are excellent conductors that rapidly transfer thermal energy.
A drawn bowstring stores elastic potential energy, which instantly transforms into kinetic energy the exact millisecond you release the arrow.
When you rub your hands together on a cold day, your muscles transform chemical energy into kinetic energy, and friction converts it into heat.
